original_card.question: Can a template or call contract leave two or more unpaid coordinates per live family?
methods: State a replacement for the coverage identity (mass = 72W + 64N) and the contract change that realizes it, with its implementation cost.
Find an obstruction: show which data-endpoint obligation forces exactly one unpaid coordinate in the current template.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An explicit replacement identity, verified on a small complete instance with dirty inputs, priced with ceiling.ceiling(unpaid=...).

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Explain where the single unpaid coordinate per family comes from in the hosted template; propose one change and price it. Ideal budget: two unpaid coordinates per family is 3.77x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: The deficit is one coordinate per family minus the centre charge; doubling unpaid coordinates per family scales it directly.
allowed_variations: One template change or one endpoint-contract change.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Counting a coordinate as unpaid while leaving it unadvanced in the data endpoint.

actual_scope: Audit the k-dimensional port-group decoders published in PR2297 (k=5) and PR2041 (k=3) as scalar decoders of the k-unpaid endpoint: F2 identity replay, k-group mask census, literal-lift and parity-forced forbidden entries, dirty scalar replay, forced rank, and budgets (philippeVV's 2-integral floor applied to the k-group covers, zero-saving and incumbent-tie thresholds in ceiling.py).
scope_change_reason: Seed 51 (recursive interfaces); the card's open k-group decoder claims (PR2297 reports an a=1/99 favourable screen) had no audit; the card's 'find an obstruction' method applied to them.
bottleneck_link: A second unpaid coordinate per family is the coverage-law lever (x3.77 ideal); its viability rests on decoder cost. The published k-group decoders do not satisfy the scalar endpoint, so their charges do not price the lever.
stop_rule: Stop after the two published certificates are replayed against the required mask with controls, and the direct decoder is priced; no search for new decoders.
evidence: verify.py (receipt pinned): both F2 identities reproduce B0; PR2297: 0 free ordered pairs, 12,281 forbidden nonzero literal entries (6,608 parity-forced), 112/112 dirty columns fail, rank >= 112 vs 16 terms, 2-integral floor 554 > zero-saving 497.8/492.4 (tie 455-460); PR2041: 102 free pairs, 11,755 forbidden (6,608 parity-forced), 112/112 fail, rank >= 99 vs 11 terms, floor 334 > 298.7/296.9 (tie 256-261). Port-space charges of the published terms: 144 and 99.

open_questions.question: Can a decoder with even-denominator gain above ~56 (any saving) or ~94 (incumbent tie) realise the diagonal rank-112 scalar map required under the k=5 mask?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the only remaining route for the u=5 contract; every 2-integral decoder costs at least 554.

open_questions.question: Can even-denominator terms exploit PR2041's 102 free pairs for gain above ~35 (any saving) or ~73 (incumbent tie)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Free-pair sharing alone cannot help any 2-integral decoder (floor 334 > 298.7).
